description: Drama Years 5-6 width tiers — ACARA v9. All strands are capability strands; primary axis is task_contexts.
subject: Drama

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest floor for the command term. For Y5-6, minimum involves one task context in which character development, element combination, rehearsal or analysis is demonstrated.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope from elaborations — the range of contexts and forms a well-taught Y5-6 class would engage with.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment adding new task types, cultural contexts, form types or analytical perspectives — not harder versions of the same activity.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations are the primary source. First Nations elaborations for E02 appear in wider; others include First Nations directions where indicated.

AC9ADR6C01.minimum_width: Student develops a character with at least two consistent characterisation choices (voice and physical) and sustains dramatic action across a short piece with a recognisable beginning, complication and resolution.
AC9ADR6C01.typical_width: Students develop characters and situations across improvised, devised and scripted forms; they use voice (projection, dynamics, pace, pause, pitch) and movement/gesture to communicate character; they rehearse and negotiate with others; they use props, costumes and technologies as dramatic symbols; they develop drama for specific purposes (school ritual, community issue).
wider: Students devise drama based on research about a school or local community project, using drama to present different perspectives in a debate or on an environmental issue
Students collaborate to devise drama for a specific school or community ritual (assembly, ceremony, health campaign) with a defined purpose and audience
Students use Viewpoints questions to evaluate their own drama: 'How did performers use elements effectively? What was the purpose? What evidence supports your judgement?'
elaborations: exploring physical, fictional or emotional spaces to create characters
varying voice using projection, dynamics, pace, pause and pitch to communicate character intentions
rehearsing, interacting and negotiating with others to interpret scripts and create characters
devising drama based on research about a school/community project for cultural awareness or debate
working collaboratively to devise drama for a school ritual or gathering
using Viewpoints to ask questions when exploring character

AC9ADR6D01.minimum_width: Student makes at least one element combination choice informed by a specific character perspective, and can explain how it communicates that perspective.
AC9ADR6D01.typical_width: Students experiment with empathy to develop characters and relationships; they compare how improvised and scripted drama create characters differently; they use Viewpoints to explore how cultures shape element use; they consider how cultural understandings shape meaning through element combinations.
wider: Students imagine themselves in the time/place of a historical event and use deliberate element combinations to explore multiple character perspectives
Students investigate a specific live performance and identify element combinations, then apply one technique in their own devising
Students explore how drama from another culture uses elements to communicate ideas that Western dramatic conventions might handle differently
elaborations: experimenting with empathy to develop characters, considering situations from different perspectives and challenging stereotypes
imagining and developing a 'new scene' to include in a dramatic re-telling of a known narrative
using Viewpoints to ask questions about cultures and element use
using improvisation or process drama to compare ways improvised and scripted drama create characters
imagining being in the time/place of a historical event and considering why people made certain decisions

AC9ADR6E01.minimum_width: Student identifies and describes how at least two elements are combined in a specific drama work, and explains what they communicate.
AC9ADR6E01.typical_width: Students identify and discuss element use (space, time, language, movement, character, relationships) using Viewpoints questions; they consider how cultural understandings shape meaning; they explore drama from other places and times and discuss how it might contribute to their own drama.
wider: Students investigate a specific drama tradition from a country or region in Asia, examining its element conventions and how they reflect cultural values
Students investigate how drama is used in their own community to maintain or revitalise culture, and identify the element combinations that carry this meaning
Students compare drama from two different cultural or historical contexts, analysing how element combinations reflect distinct social purposes
elaborations: exploring how drama is used within communities to maintain, continue and revitalise culture
identifying and discussing element use using Viewpoints questions
exploring drama from other places and times and discussing how it might contribute to their own drama and how cultural understandings shape meaning

AC9ADR6E02.minimum_width: Student explains the difference between cultural maintenance and revitalisation, and describes at least two specific ways a First Nations drama maker uses drama to represent identity or community.
AC9ADR6E02.typical_width: Students explore how performances that tell stories maintain culture; they identify how cultural expressions change over time using First Nations community-published resources; they investigate how First Nations drama makers embed identity, community, storytelling and resilience across representative forms.
wider: Students investigate how First Nations drama has adapted contemporary forms (physical theatre, digital media) while maintaining cultural authority
Students investigate First Nations drama that explicitly responds to colonial history, exploring how form carries cultural and political assertion
Students compare First Nations drama from different communities, noting shared themes (land, identity, story) and distinctive cultural expressions
elaborations: exploring how performances that tell stories maintain culture
identifying and discussing the role of storytelling in First Nations cultural traditions
identifying examples showing how cultural expressions change over time
investigating how diverse First Nations drama makers embed community in drama as visual declaration of identity, storytelling and resilience

AC9ADR6P01.minimum_width: Student participates in at least two purposeful rehearsal sessions and performs in one informal or formal setting with sustained communicative intent, using at least one technical element.
AC9ADR6P01.typical_width: Students understand and demonstrate rehearsal purpose and collaboration; they remember lines, moves and cues; they use props, costumes and technologies as dramatic symbols; they share ideas with audiences through performance choices or introductions; they perform in informal and formal settings.
wider: Students devise and perform drama for a specific community audience (school assembly, cultural event), adapting content and form for purpose
Students create a pre-show presentation — podcast, programme note, or poster — that frames the drama for their audience
Students evaluate their performance against rehearsal intentions, noting what communicated as intended and what they would change
elaborations: using props, costumes and technologies to create dramatic symbols and enhance dramatic action
focusing on communication with audience — remembering lines, moves and cues
showing understanding of the purpose of rehearsing and the need for collaboration
sharing ideas about their drama with audiences through performance space choice, approach to entering/leaving the space, or pre-show presentations
